snippet.title: Lucky Fight Vs. Ika Musume 3X [らき☆ふぁいVSイカ娘３Ｘ] Game Sample - PC/Doujin
snippet.description:
Another rare Doujin for the day, we have the definitive version of the base game, "Lucky Fighter II", which is a huge improvement that took five years to come to fruition. 

Developed by D.C.S. with collaboration from mokonaXVI (MokonaPuu), the game is a much more proper clone of Capcom's "Pocket Fighter" (aka "Super Gem Fighter Mini-Mix") and there's a bit of a funny story to go with this one. I probably wouldn't have this one if it wasn't for a fellow YouTuber, EX Falchion, a fighting game enthusiast who has been looking for the game for so long that he contacted one of the creators (Mokona of all people) who agreed to put his private copy of the game up for auction. While I'd heard of the game for a while, none of the iterations of the game hardly ever show up for sale and, unbeknownst to both of us, when the game did show, a fierce bidding war began to acquire the elusive game. A few days and $250 dollars later, I wound up getting the game. However, I intend to preserve the game for future gamers, so it's a win-win for everybody.

The game uses the same engine as their previous fighting games, so it's kinda wonky and the only way I could capture the game on a modern system was to switch the game to 16-bit color mode, force window the game using DxWnd and then record with OBS. Once configured, it works fine enough with no major issues. The game recognizes controller inputs fine and has a dedicated training mode now (LFII had one, but it was semi-hidden). The game features twelve playable characters with --- acting as a boss character, upgraded movesets for the existing characters (with all characters now having a LV3 Super Move as well as various cosplay combos and the new launcher aerial rave system), a basic scoring system, numerous colors for each character (with a few adding additional garments or secret cut-ins such as one of Konata's racier outfits), character voices (which had to be patched in with an included update disc), new visual effects (including new stages and more particle effects for existing moves) and rebalanced gameplay (damage adjustments, A.I. adjustments, frame adjustments, etc.). It feels like an almost entirely different game.

The game still lacks an air block and still has a guard cancel system, but the expanded moveset makes it a little less bothersome. The best thing by far is using all the variations of cosplay combos to spot all the references and recognizing all the bases for each character. For example, Konata is your typical "Ryu/Ken" clone who cosplays Haruhi, Shana, etc. while Akira is "Felicia from Darkstalkers",  Minami is "Cammy", so on and so forth. As alluded to in the title, the game also has a guest appearance from Ika Musume (Squid Girl) and each character has their own theme and stage as well as intros and win quotes. Just like before, the game utilizes a SF command system with a three-button setup (Punch / Kick / Charge or Super) and hitting opponents knocks gems out of them that can be grabbed to restore bits of lost health and upgrade your special attacks up to level 3. It's worth noting that you only get one chance to clear the game -- losing both rounds results in a Game Over and a restart for the player.

While I wouldn't say it's the best Doujin fighter I've played, it's definitely the best one by D.C.S. so far and also deserves some accolades for being one of the most competent Lucky Star fan games. This is a video showing a playthrough with Akira, one attraction and a basic combo demonstration for all the characters (except Akira, as she got enough time during gameplay). Enjoy.
